speaker: client
text: For V1, what simple, reliable implementation approach would you use for the spout? It must provide a smooth, controlled pour while remaining easy to clean between uses. A proper seal should prevent liquid from leaking into the base, and the open/close mechanism needs to operate cleanly without dripping.

speaker: client
text:
Key Design Details

1\. Valve / flow control — I need a simple open/close valve or tap that prevents constant dripping and uncontrolled pouring.

2\. Seal at the bottom — This is critical: the bottom bowl seal must prevent external leaks as well as seepage into the electronics.

3\. Cleaning — Because matcha + milk leaves residue, the spout should either be removable or easy to flush and clean.

4\. Flow rate — I need a smooth, controlled stream rather than a slow drip or an explosive pour.

speaker: freelancer
text: Although this is a significant change to the engineering scope, I can make it work. I haven’t been able to find an off-the-shelf spout that closely matches the appearance of the one in your renders, but I did find an option that should function well. A solenoid valve would sit directly beneath the bowl, preventing any matcha from entering the spout until the button is pressed; releasing the button would stop the pour. Since no matcha would remain in either the spout or the tubing, its frothiness will be maintained. Please review this option: <https://www.amazon.com/Stainless-Pourers-BALTRE-Vinegar-Suitable> Alternatively, if keeping the appearance of the original rendered spout is more important, I could fabricate a custom version, though it would not be made from steel.

speaker: client
text: Go ahead with that approach, and please match the rendering as closely as possible; I really like both its appearance and functionality. I do want one change from the rendering: move the plate labeled "Elena's Chai Whisk" from the back of the machine to the front. The spout and mixers will face the baristas, while customers will view the machine from another angle, so the "Elena's Chai Whisk" plate needs to face the customer.

speaker: client
text:
I’m good with this direction because the additional power and adjustable speed range make sense. The 5200 RPM motors work for me as long as we do not run them at maximum continuously; being able to dial them down for slow mixing or increase them for higher-speed frothing is ideal.

With that higher maximum, however, we need to ensure two things:
• splashing remains under control
• mixing stays smooth rather than becoming overly aggressive at higher speeds

If necessary, I’m open to adding a splash guard or adjusting the whisk position and bowl depth so the machine continues to operate cleanly. Overall, I approve this approach.

speaker: freelancer
text: Elena, the machine is sturdy, and everything is functioning as expected. During testing, however, I found a leak in one piece of the plumbing that I still need to repair.
